verdicts.note: No abstract. Mandate exposure, perinatal outcomes.
FERTILITY-PRESERVATION insurance mandates. An access-margin paper sitting inside Wall 5's medical half: the exposure is A.17-shaped, the population is oncofertility. Boundary case worth an RA look.
Access to treatment plus economic valuation of live births.
No abstract; title decisive. Mandates and racial/ethnic inequities in ART utilisation.
Diminished ovarian reserve diagnosis and treatment; mandate status is a covariate.
No abstract; title decisive on outcome (marriage and childbearing timing). Exposure specification not visible.
Student attitudes, Turkey vs US.
Mandates and disparities in DONOR-OOCYTE ART specifically — a distinct treatment margin.
Ovarian reserve biology.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW of global infertility insurance coverage. A channel-1 record: it maps the international access variation the chapter needs and may spare a lot of hand-sourcing.
Early pregnancy complications and completed family size. B.5's (fetal loss) — route there.
Industry news digest summarising a primary study. Chase the target, not this record.
Menken, Science 1986 — the age-infertility curve estimated on historical natural-fertility populations. Not an A.17 estimate; it is the parameter every P4 simulation rests on.
Educational enrolment as the driver of postponement.
NBER 2025 overview of low fertility in high-income countries. Relevant to the review as a whole, not to A.17's cell.
Serbia, postponement and biology.
PDR 2026: infertility's role in unrealized ideal family size. Not an ART estimate, but it BOUNDS what any recovery arm could deliver — the ceiling on A.17's claim.

ISRAEL, UNLIMITED PUBLICLY FUNDED ACCESS: IVF among women 40-44 rose sharply 2011-2014 while AGE-SPECIFIC BIRTH RATES DID NOT SUBSTANTIALLY CHANGE. Directly on the chapter's central question and pointing the opposite way to v5. Priority full-text.
Russia. Tag SECONDARY under Wall 8.

A letter, but it names a target worth chasing: an estimate of the contribution of NON-ART ovulation stimulation to US singleton and multiple births. A.12 found ovulation induction drives 40-70% of high-order multiples through a channel single-embryo-transfer policy does not touch, and the Australian data in batch 1 split MAR into 4.8% ART and 1.9% OI.
Commentary on reproductive ageing.
Early-life disease and lifetime childlessness, Finland/Sweden.
State panel: adoption against ART utilisation. Second record in the frame on ART-adoption substitution. Off-estimand, but the substitution margin is exactly what makes arm 1's count an upper bound.

AEJ:APPLIED 2020. Israel's 1994 adoption of FREE IVF as a natural experiment. The cleanest access shock in the frame — universal, sharp, national. Reported outcomes here are marriage timing and career; whether births are reported must be settled at full text. Priority.
Fertility beyond 40 — the age band where ART's share is largest (16% in the Italian data).
No abstract. Medicaid vs private coverage and treatment use — an insurance-type margin distinct from state mandates.
Preprint of the Nature Human Behaviour childlessness paper.
Discourse analysis of news framing.
Finnish students, awareness of age effects.
JPE 1980 dynamic model of birth timing.
Ethics commentary on coverage and reproductive autonomy.
Fertility awareness among migrant women in Germany.
No abstract; title decisive. CONSUMER AFFORDABILITY against ART access, international. Cross-country price variation is the access margin with the most leverage and the least US-specificity.
Tempo-adjusted parity progression measures. Methodological, and it bears on PI call 4: which fertility measure ART's contribution is expressed against.
Systematic review of knowledge of age-related fertility decline.
Danish conception rates and male reproductive health. B.2/B.6's.
Public perception of ART funding across 6 European countries. Attitudes to the policy, not its effect.
Descriptive analysis of rising childlessness.
Qualitative interviews, childless women 34-39.
HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS' poor knowledge of age-related decline and of ART's limits. If the advisers overestimate ART too, the belief channel has a supply side.
JAMA 2017, CDC surveillance: proportion of US live births attributable to ART by maternal age. A core arm-1 record and the US counterpart to the Italian and Australian shares.
Families and Societies WP4 report on childlessness and ART in Europe.
'TECHNOLOGY MYTHS' — lay beliefs about what ART can undo. This is P6's mechanism named directly rather than fertility knowledge in general.
Pakistan; tag SECONDARY under Wall 8.
Fiscal value of ART-conceived children in Australia. It does count them, but the outcome is public finance.

Demography 2021 microsimulation of Dutch childlessness through union transitions. Third Dutch microsimulation in the frame — the group is prolific and its assumptions should be assessed once, jointly.
Wartime fertility intentions, Ukraine.
Sterility and childbearing in second unions, France. Bears on repartnering as an alternative route to the same births.
University students' fertility awareness.
Evaluates INTERVENTIONS to raise awareness — the closest P6 gets to a manipulation, alongside the RCT in batch 2.
Academic promotion and childbearing, Italy. C.2.e's.

**THE FIRST P5 RECORD WITH A FERTILITY OUTCOME rather than an attitude.** Elective oocyte banking modelled as a strategy for expanding the fertile lifespan. Everything else in the elective cell so far measures what women think about egg freezing, not what it produces.
Airborne lead and the general fertility rate. B.2's, and well identified.
Working-paper version of the Israel free-IVF natural experiment. Version-of-record duplicate with the AEJ:Applied record — flag.
Young men's fertility knowledge, UK 2026.
Post-myomectomy fertility, Burkina Faso.
Regional age-pattern of fertility in southern Russia.
te Velde on the VARIABILITY of reproductive ageing — the dispersion that decides how much of the age-related loss ART can address at all.
Social age deadlines for childbearing across countries — perceived deadlines against biological ones.
ASRM committee opinion.
